headline: 60 kmph winds expected: Storms and heavy rain hit 15 districts including Dhaka
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department warns of strong winds and increased rainfall over the next five days across several regions.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has issued a warning for 15 districts, including Dhaka, forecasting storms with wind speeds of up to 60 kmph.
A powerful rain belt is moving in, with four divisions expected to be most active, bringing significant rainfall to various parts of the country.
The BMD further predicts that rainfall is likely to increase over the next five days, potentially affecting daily activities and travel.
Residents in the affected districts are advised to be cautious of sudden storms and heavy downpours as the weather system intensifies.

headline: BGB and locals foil BSF push-in bid at Lalmonirhat border
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh and villagers thwarted an attempt by India's BSF to force 10-12 individuals into Bangladeshi territory last night.
details: An alleged attempt by India's Border Security Force (BSF) to push a group of 10 to 12 individuals into Bangladesh was thwarted at the Amjhol border in Lalmonirhat's Hatibandha upazila.
The incident occurred around 8:30 PM near Sub-Pillar No. 8 of Main Border Pillar No. 906, when a vehicle carrying the group arrived at the border.
According to the Lalmonirhat BGB Battalion-15 media cell, BSF members from the Paglamari Camp allegedly tried to force the individuals through a gate in the barbed-wire fence.
Local residents noticed the unusual activity and raised an alarm using loudspeakers, which quickly drew hundreds of villagers to the site.
Faced with the combined presence of hundreds of civilians and BGB personnel, the BSF members reportedly withdrew and took the individuals back from the zero line.
Lt Col Mehedi Imam, commanding officer of Lalmonirhat BGB Battalion-15, confirmed the incident and stated that BGB is operating at the highest level of alert.
He added that round-the-clock surveillance has been strengthened in the border area to safeguard the country's sovereignty and border security.
caption:
Hundreds of villagers and BGB personnel joined forces to stop an alleged BSF 'push-in' attempt at the Lalmonirhat border.

An alleged attempt by India's Border Security Force (BSF) to push a group of 10 to 12 individuals into Bangladesh was thwarted at the Amjhol border in Lalmonirhat's Hatibandha upazila.

The incident occurred around 8:30 PM near Sub-Pillar No. 8 of Main Border Pillar No. 906, when a vehicle carrying the group arrived at the border.

According to the Lalmonirhat BGB Battalion-15 media cell, BSF members from the Paglamari Camp allegedly tried to force the individuals through a gate in the barbed-wire fence.

Local residents noticed the unusual activity and raised an alarm using loudspeakers, which quickly drew hundreds of villagers to the site.

Faced with the combined presence of hundreds of civilians and BGB personnel, the BSF members reportedly withdrew and took the individuals back from the zero line.

Lt Col Mehedi Imam, commanding officer of Lalmonirhat BGB Battalion-15, confirmed the incident and stated that BGB is operating at the highest level of alert.

He added that round-the-clock surveillance has been strengthened in the border area to safeguard the country's sovereignty and border security.
